project.name: Shadow AI Capture
project.summary: Records what employees send to generative AI tools from company-managed devices, and makes it queryable - with content interpreted on the device by default and crossing the network only on an explicit per-event grant.
project.testCommand: psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f db/schema.sql && psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -f db/invariants.test.sql

components.name: Capture Extension
components.summary: Web-request and request-body inspection in the browser: wide observation, narrow emission, inline warn/block.
components.notes: Not yet built. Owns the browser half of the nine usage modes.

components.name: Capture Core
components.runtime: one static binary per platform, MSI/PKG
components.summary: Egress proxy provider, loopback inference broker, process and model detector, CLI trust shim, policy engine, and the encrypted bounded spool.
components.notes: The single place device-side policy is enforced.

components.name: Classifier Host
components.runtime: native and wasm32 from one source
components.summary: Rules, then validators, then a model; document parsing in a child process. Decides what the event means without the content leaving the machine.
components.notes: One source compiled twice: native for the device, wasm32 for in-page use.

components.name: Event Envelope Contract
components.summary: The single wire contract. A discriminated union with a closed kind registry; observations are immutable and the envelope is the record.
components.notes: The only artifact every other component already agrees on.

components.name: Ingest API
components.summary: Events only, no keys. Owns device authentication, idempotency, the dedup tie-break and the rejection reason codes.
components.notes: ingest.record_event() is the one write path; collectors hold no database credential.

components.name: Control API
components.summary: Enrolment, policy, grants and health - everything that is not an event.
components.notes: Grant issuance is what makes content cross the network, one event at a time.

components.name: Content Vault
components.summary: The only component that can unwrap content keys. Retrieval and, at full_text, the content search index.
components.notes: Reachable from inside the network only; never from the internet.

components.name: Query API
components.summary: The browser never speaks SQL: a closed query DSL compiles to parameterised queries, with audit-on-read and k-suppression.

components.name: Dashboard
components.summary: The ten questions, answered from aggregates, with cursor pagination and an export path.

components.name: Aggregator
components.summary: Replace-the-bucket upserts that keep the mart aggregates fresh, and the retention materialisation.

components.name: PostgreSQL Schema
components.runtime: Azure Database for PostgreSQL 16 Flexible Server
components.summary: 34 tables, 3 views and 28 row-level security policies across ref, ops, ingest and mart schemas, with roles, triggers, functions and seed data.
components.notes: The schema and its 27 assertions were executed against a real server as the runtime roles, not as a superuser.

components.name: Device Spool
components.summary: A bounded, encrypted, on-device queue. SQLite is the device store and nothing else.

components.name: Azure Infrastructure
components.summary: Front Door Premium + WAF, Private Link, environments, endpoint distribution and signing, update rings, SLOs and the cost model.

components.name: Design Package
components.summary: The master document, six subsystem documents, fifteen ADRs, the wire contract and the database - with every constraint traced to the brief.
components.notes: This is the current state of the project: a design package, not a built system.

tasks.subject: Generate TypeScript and Go types from the envelope contract
tasks.description: The contract exists; nothing consumes it yet. Every other component depends on this shape being stable and generated rather than hand-copied.

tasks.subject: Stand up the PostgreSQL schema and prove its invariants
tasks.description: Run db/schema.sql then db/invariants.test.sql against a real PostgreSQL 16 server as the runtime roles. The 27 assertions are the acceptance criteria.

tasks.subject: Implement the ingest write path and the two-tier dedup ladder
tasks.description: ingest.record_event() owns idempotency, the dedup tie-break and retention, enforced by partial unique indices per docs/02-ingest-and-transport.md section 4.

tasks.subject: Implement the closed query DSL and the read path
tasks.description: The browser must never speak SQL. A closed DSL compiles to parameterised queries, with audit-on-read and k-suppression, per ADR 0003.

tasks.subject: Implement the content vault key hierarchy and grant-bound retrieval
tasks.description: Per-object content keys wrapped by a per-tenant key; the only component that can unwrap. Grant issuance is per event and recorded.

tasks.subject: Validate local-inference capture, which gates build step 8
tasks.description: Brief risk R1. A validation task, not a design task: measure whether the loopback inference broker sees what the design assumes it sees on both operating systems.

tasks.subject: Resolve the organisational dimension, without which three headline questions cannot be answered
tasks.description: Brief risk Q2. Decide where the org dimension comes from and record it, then amend the affected read paths.

agents.purpose: Keeps the wire contract the single source of shape, and generates the language bindings from it.
agents.task: Generate TypeScript and Go types from contracts/event-envelope.schema.json. Do not hand-edit generated output, and do not widen the closed kind registry without an ADR.
agents.notes: The only agent allowed to touch contracts/. Everyone else reads it.

agents.purpose: Owns the schema, the row-level security policies and the invariants that prove them.
agents.task: Apply db/schema.sql and db/invariants.test.sql to a real PostgreSQL 16 server and make all 27 assertions hold as the runtime roles - never as a superuser, which would bypass RLS and prove nothing.
agents.notes: Residency is pinned and fails closed at ingest; the schema is where that is enforced.

agents.purpose: Builds the one validating write path and the dedup ladder behind it.
agents.task: Implement ingest-api and ingest.record_event(): device authentication, idempotency, the two-tier dedup tie-break, retention and the rejection reason codes. Collectors must end up holding no database credential.
agents.notes: The normative dedup specification is docs/02-ingest-and-transport.md section 4.

agents.purpose: Builds the closed query DSL and the dashboard read path.
agents.task: Implement query-api's closed query DSL compiling to parameterised queries, with audit-on-read and k-suppression, then the dashboard that asks it the ten questions.
agents.notes: The browser never speaks SQL - the DSL is closed, not escaped.

agents.purpose: Owns the key hierarchy and the only component permitted to unwrap content.
agents.task: Implement content-vault: per-object content keys wrapped by a per-tenant key, internal ingress only, and retrieval bound to a recorded per-event grant. Content is ciphertext at rest and the vault is the only unwrapper.
agents.notes: The mutually exclusive pair - customer-held keys with server-side content search - is a database check constraint, not a policy note.

agents.purpose: Closes the three brief risks that are validation tasks rather than design tasks.
agents.task: Measure whether the loopback inference broker captures local model traffic as the design assumes, on both operating systems, and record the answer with the evidence. Then close Q2 (the organisational dimension).
agents.notes: R1 gates build step 8; Q1 (residency) and Q2 are the other two on the critical path.

invariants.statement: Content stays put by default: the only content-egress path is a per-event grant, so uploading everything is structurally unreachable rather than merely forbidden.
One validating write path: collectors hold no database credential, and every event is validated once, in one place.
One read path: the browser never speaks SQL; a closed DSL compiles to parameterised queries.
Observations are immutable - history cannot be rewritten by anyone short of a superuser.
Isolation is structural: forced row-level security, tenant-leading keys, and per-tenant content keys as an independent second layer.
Coverage is honest: every collection path reports its own health, so a path that is not working appears as degraded or absent, never as an absence of data.
